aspects.says: An advice reports what already happened and is acknowledged, never declined; until then it is repeated with the fourth digit set to 1 and nothing else changed, so a receiver must answer repeats as it answers the original.

aspects.says: The MTI pairs kinds of message, so a response belongs to a request only when it also carries the request's STAN and terminal ID.

aspects.says: The class digit decides what an approval commits: an 0100 holds the amount, an 0200 posts the debit, and an 0800 touches no account, so an unanswered echo needs no clean-up.

aspects.says: The four MTI digits name the edition, the class, the function and the origin, in every edition.

aspects.says: A reversal is a new message with its own STAN that names the original in field 90: its MTI, STAN, field 7 and the institution IDs zero-filled to eleven digits.

aspects.says: A request without an answer is reversed, never sent again, because the acquirer cannot tell whether it was approved and a second request is a second purchase.

aspects.says: A message's answer keeps its class and raises the function digit by one, so a request is answered by a response and an advice by an advice response, and a repeat is answered like the message it repeats.
